QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS ON CORONAVIRUS PT. 2

Is there a vaccine for coronavirus?

When a disease is new, there is no vaccine until one is developed. It can take a number of years for a new vaccine to be developed.

Is there a treatment for a novel coronavirus?

There is no specific treatment for disease caused by a novel coronavirus. However, many of the symptoms can be treated and therefore treatment based on the patient’s clinical condition. Moreover, supportive care for infected persons can be highly effective.

What can I do to protect myself?

Standard recommendations to reduce exposure to and transmission of a range of illnesses include maintaining basic hand and respiratory hygiene, and safe food practices  and avoiding close contact, when possible, with anyone showing symptoms of respiratory illness such as coughing and sneezing.

Prevention

Currently there are no vaccines available to protect against human coronavirus infection but the risk of infection can be reduced by proper washing of hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, avoid touching your eyes, nose, or mouth with unwashed hands and avoid close contact with people who are infected.

Protect others when you have cold-like symptoms and these can be done by isolating yourself from coming in contact with non-infected people while sick, covering your mouth and nose with a tissue when you cough or sneeze, and then discard the tissue into the trash and properly wash your hands and clean and disinfect objects and surfaces.

Treatment

There are no specific treatments for human coronaviruses. Most people with common human coronavirus illness recover on their own. However, some things can be done to relieve your symptoms by taking prescribed pain and fever medications, use a room humidifier, taking a hot shower to help ease sore throat and cough.

Also when sick, drink plenty of liquids and stay at home and rest.

Coronaviruses (CoV)

What are Coronaviruses (CoV)?
Coronaviruses (CoV) are a large family of viruses that cause illness ranging from the common cold to more severe diseases such as Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS-CoV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS-CoV). A novel coronavirus (nCoV) is a new strain that has not been previously identified in humans.

Transmission Process:
Coronaviruses are zoonotic, meaning they are transmitted between animals and people.
Detailed investigations found that SARS-CoV was transmitted from civet cats to humans and MERS-CoV from dromedary camels to humans. Several known coronaviruses are circulating in animals that have not yet infected humans.

Common Signs and Symptoms:
Respiratory symptoms, fever, cough, shortness of breath and breathing difficulties. In more severe cases, infection can cause pneumonia, severe acute respiratory syndrome, kidney failure and even death.

Prevention Measures:
Regular hand washing, covering mouth and nose when coughing and sneezing, thoroughly cooking meat and eggs. Avoid close contact with anyone showing symptoms of respiratory illness such as coughing and sneezing. (WHO)

How to protect yourself from coronavirus 🤔 - 🧼👋 Wash your hands: wet your hands with clean, running water and apply soap. Lather your hands, including the backs, between your fingers, and under your nails and scrub for at least 20 seconds. - 🗣 🤭 Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue when you cough or sneeze, then throw the tissue in the bin and wash your hands. If you do not have a tissue to hand, cough or sneeze into your elbow rather than your hands. - 😷 😷 Face masks offer some protection as they block liquid droplets. However, they do not block smaller aerosol particles that can pass through the material of the mask. The masks also leave the eyes exposed and there is evidence that some viruses can infect a person through the eyes. 👀 - 👨‍⚕️👩‍⚕️ Seek early medical help if you have a fever, cough and difficulty breathing, and share your travel history with healthcare providers. - 🐖 🐄 If visiting live markets in affected areas avoid direct, unprotected contact with live animals and surfaces that have been in contact with animals. .

WHAT IS CORONAVIRUS 
Coronavirus are zoonotic, meaning they are transmitted between animals and humans. 
Coronaviruses are common in many different species of animals, including camels and bats. Rarely, these coronaviruses can evolve and infect humans and then spread between humans. 
SYMPTOMS *Fever
*Coughing
*Chills
*Headache
*Difficulty breathing,
*Sore throat

How it spreads:
The virus can be transmitted between people through respiratory droplets such as saliva or mucus. 
It may be passed before a person shows symptoms.

What is coronavirus?

According to the WHO, coronaviruses are a family of viruses that cause illness ranging from the common cold to more severe diseases such as SARS and Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS).
These viruses were originally transmitted between animals and people. SARS, for instance, was believed to have been transmitted from civet cats to humans while MERS travelled from a type of camel to humans.
Several known coronaviruses are circulating in animals that have not yet infected humans.
The name coronavirus comes from the Latin word corona, meaning crown or halo. Under an electron microscope, the image of the virus is reminiscent of a solar corona.

We can catch virus by touching our face, especially the conjunctiva of the eyes (Dr. Scott Gottlieb on Feb 03, 2020 CNBC Special Report Coronavirus). A demonstration by Glo-Germ powder, visible only under a blacklight is part of a well-known educational dramatization in a classroom. An hour after powdering a couple of kids' hands with Glo-Germ, all the kids have the powder on their hands and faces. Indeed we rub faces and eyes without being aware of it. So an idea of boosting self-awareness consists of applying on the fingers a sort of harmless but eyes-"burning" cream containing a capsaicinoid. Even slightly touching an eye with the fingers quickly activates the heat-sensitive receptors. After "burning" the eye once, the bad habit of touching the eyes may become broken. Capsaicinoids are the active ingredient of red chili pepper and bear-deterrent and law enforcement sprays and heat creams.

Prevention is better than cure…….Protect yourselves from the Corona Virus

Corona virus—a large group of viruses common in animals and rarely transmitted from animals to humans.  The virus makes people sick, usually mild to moderate upper respiratory tract illness, like common cold.

How it spreads—spreads from an infected person to others through:
Through air by coughing and sneezing
Personal contact-touching or shaking hands
Touching an infected object or surface & then touching your mouth, nose, eyes without washing hands
Very rarely faecal contamination

Symptoms—very similar to common cold
Runny nose, headache
Sore throat, cough
Fever
Feeling of being unwell

If the immune system is weak, especially in elderly & children, it may lead to bronchitis or pneumonia.

Prevention—As of now, NO vaccines are available for protection against human coronavirus infection.  So, prevention is the best.  Some tips are :

1.Wash your hands before touching food, your mouth, nose or eyes-maintain personal hygiene.
2. Avoid any form of cold drinks, ice creams, cold coffees etc
Avoid any type of preserved foods, milkshakes, ice colas, sweets older than 48hours
3. Avoid close contact with people who are sick
If mildly sick, keep yourself hydrated, stay at home & rest
If concerned about your symptoms, consult your doctor.
4. Drink boiled water, stop non-veg
5. Take vitamin C, Zinc, B complex daily for prevention
Decoction of Tulsi, Ginger, Pepper, Turmeric helps immensely
Guduchi ghanavati treats fever & enhances immunity
6. Drink hot rasam or soups through the day
